value.rationale: The natural deviation-rate observable of random projection widths is exactly zero for bodies of constant width, but no positive-height orthogonal prism in ambient dimension \(d\ge3\) has constant width. The theorem quantifies the unavoidable minimum sharply over an infinite-dimensional class of arbitrary base shapes, classifies the complete equality shapes and optimal height, supplies an exact nonnegative two-defect rigidity formula, and determines the nontrivial Gaussian \(d^2\)-scaling constant. This is a motivated complete geometric extremal classification rather than an isolated numerical value. Risk: the core finite-dimensional calculation is elementary once the correct product parametrization is chosen; its interest rests on class-wide sharpness, stability and high-d behavior.
